statement_summary: Program documented; CIP controls for Critical Cyber Systems
Cybersecurity and Security Coordinators designated; TSA told within 7 and 37 days of change
Annual SP 800-30 risk assessment coordinated with the hazmat plan review
Risk acceptance authority; no safety-linked risk accepted above Low
CIP milestones kept; TSA told before a miss; amendments within 50 days
Quarterly audit committee reporting
Annual 1580.101 applicability check; directive review within 30 days
Annual policy and standard review
Written, time-limited exceptions that do not conflict with the CIP
Annual independent assessment; one-third of CIP measures each year; architecture review every 2 years
Proportionate sanctions; collective bargaining procedures apply
Vendor security review and contract terms; company keeps CIP responsibility
Annual reassessment of Tier 1 vendors
Retention of security records at least 5 years
AI tools approved before use; no AI replaces an FRA-required inspection
Unique accounts; shared accounts only where critical and vaulted; no shared dispatcher logins
Shared passwords changed at each departure and yearly
Least privilege; separation of maintainer and CAD/CTC administrator rights
MFA everywhere supported; phishing-resistant for administrators; documented OT exceptions
Same-day disable at termination; tablets, applications, and badges within 24 hours
Remove prior-role access within 5 business days of transfer
Quarterly access and application role reviews; yearly trust review
Separate privileged accounts with just-in-time elevation and recording
Lockout and session lock; console exception documented in the CIP
Break-glass accounts sealed and tested quarterly
14-character passwords; reset on compromise; default credentials changed
Vendor remote access only through the PAM jump host; no always-on paths
Field housings locked or sealed; key control; quarterly badge review
Incident response plan and runbooks with positions and resources
Report suspected incidents immediately and within 1 hour
Incident log with identification time and classification against the directive definition
CISA report within 72 hours naming the directive; 24-hour company target
TSA report of a cyber attack within 24 hours; TSOC call within 12 hours
SSI release, FRA, hazmat, and PTC failure reports; breach notices

Containment objectives and evidence preservation
Backups scanned when made and when restored
30-minute RSSM answer continues during outages
Ransom decision by the CEO with OFAC check
Annual exercise testing 2 objectives with named positions; isolation every 2 years
Role-based incident training for dispatch, PTC, signal, and MSSP staff
Lessons learned within 30 days
Four classes including SSI
SSI in the restricted library; need to know; vendor records; quarterly review
SSI marking, destruction, and marking check before filing
Prompt report to TSA of SSI release
Hazmat security plan on a need-to-know basis
Encryption at rest and in transit; OT over IT encrypted
Daily write-once backups; scanning; quarterly restore tests
Retention schedule including RSSM chain of custody and training records
Sanitization of media including retired OT and tablets
Shared service data segregated and returned per agreement
No Restricted data, SSI, or imagery in unapproved AI
Operational consoles for operational use only
Annual awareness training; TSA security training within 60 days
Approved software only; allowlisting; macros blocked
No personal devices or media on company networks or equipment
Crew tablets locked and losses reported within 1 hour
Report phishing and suspected incidents
No disclosure of SSI or security details; verify callers
Approved AI tools only, by data class; human review
No bypassing of security controls, locks, or seals
System use notice
